clinicalPearls: Caused by haploinsufficiency of PHIP, a protein that acts within a chromatin-modifying complex where its bromodomain and WD40 repeats help read and organise histone modifications, linking the disorder to the epigenetic machinery
The recognisable combination is intellectual disability or developmental delay with obesity and behavioural difficulties
Behavioural features often include attention-deficit hyperactivity, anxiety and autistic traits
A characteristic facial appearance may include a high or broad forehead, downslanting palpebral fissures and a prominent nasal bridge
Additional findings can include hypotonia, short stature, ophthalmological problems and, in some, structural anomalies
Because obesity is a core feature, weight, metabolic health and associated complications should be monitored over time
Diagnosis is confirmed by identifying a loss-of-function PHIP variant or a deletion involving the gene
reference.pathophysiology: PHIP encodes a component of a chromatin-associated complex that, through its bromodomain and WD40 repeat structures, recognises modified histones and helps regulate access to chromatin and the expression of downstream genes. Loss-of-function variants and deletions reduce the available protein (haploinsufficiency), disturbing this chromatin-reading function and the gene-expression programmes it supports, including those influencing neurodevelopment and the central regulation of appetite and energy balance. The resulting dysregulation manifests as developmental delay and intellectual disability with a characteristic behavioural profile, alongside a predisposition to obesity, positioning the condition within the broader group of Mendelian disorders of the epigenetic machinery.
additionalDifferentials: Prader-Willi syndrome and other genomic imprinting obesity syndromes
MC4R and other monogenic obesity disorders
Other syndromic intellectual disability with obesity
Non-specific autism spectrum disorder with intellectual disability
additionalInvestigations: Exome or genome sequencing to detect PHIP variants
Chromosomal microarray to identify deletions involving PHIP
Growth and body mass index monitoring with metabolic screening for obesity-related complications
Neurodevelopmental and behavioural assessment including attention and autism evaluation
Assessment for hypotonia and feeding in infancy
Brain MRI if structural anomalies or seizures are suspected
redFlags: Rapidly progressive obesity with emerging metabolic complications
Obstructive sleep apnoea related to obesity
Significant behavioural disturbance affecting safety or function
reference.prognosis: Life expectancy is not clearly reduced, but intellectual disability is usually mild to moderate and behavioural difficulties and obesity often persist, so long-term outcome is improved by early developmental support, behavioural intervention and proactive management of weight and its metabolic consequences.
pitfalls: Attributing the obesity and developmental delay to Prader-Willi syndrome without appropriate genetic testing
Overlooking treatable behavioural comorbidities such as attention-deficit hyperactivity and anxiety
Failing to monitor and address obesity-related metabolic complications
Missing small deletions of PHIP when only single-gene sequence analysis is performed
references: Nature Reviews Genetics — chromatin readers and Mendelian disorders of the epigenetic machinery
management: Early developmental intervention with speech and language, occupational and physiotherapy and individualised educational support for intellectual disability
Behavioural and psychiatric management of attention-deficit hyperactivity, anxiety and autistic traits, including stimulant or other pharmacotherapy where indicated
Proactive weight and metabolic management with dietetic input, lifestyle measures and monitoring of body mass index and obesity-related complications
Assessment and treatment of infantile hypotonia and feeding difficulties, with monitoring of growth and short stature
Ophthalmological review and correction of refractive or other ocular problems
Coordinated multidisciplinary care through clinical genetics and developmental paediatrics
Genetic counselling for this autosomal dominant PHIP disorder, with parental testing to distinguish de novo from inherited variants and family screening as indicated
